articles.headline: Notice (box of goods for the contrabands)
articles.summary: Mrs. Elizabeth Herris sent to Washington, some five weeks ago, a box of goods for the Contrabands, to the president of the Union Relief Association, Brother Green. Did he get it?

articles.headline: Appointments in the Union A. M. E. Church
articles.summary: Sunday morning, 21st inst., 10 1/2 o'clock, A.M. Third sermon of the course on "affliction." Theme, "Afflicted saints are led by the right way." Afternoon at 3 o'clock, P.M., by Rev. J. H. Smith. Evening at 8 o'clock. Subject, "The Sovereignty of God."
people: afternoon preacher at Union A.M.E. Church (Rev.)

articles.headline: Look Next Week! (visit to the Old Folks' Colored Home and the Orphan Asylum)
articles.summary: We shall give an account of our visit to the Old Folks' Colored Home, and also the Orphan Asylum. Also Rev. Mrs. French's beautiful book.

articles.headline: Letter on the churches of the Burlington Circuit
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Perhaps it would be interesting to your readers to hear how the churches on Burlington Circuit are prospering. On going to my charge, I found the church in Burlington laboring under a debt of over eleven hundred dollars, and the interest money not paid, which had been due ever since last January. (Unsigned. Collections of June 7 and June 27 at Burlington; $37 lifted at the Mount Holly Church for windows and doors of the new church, which it is hoped to consecrate this summer; the friends at Evesham have concluded to build a new church, $56 collected June 21.)

articles.headline: Colored Troops, No. 2 (letter on Sabbath recruiting in Philadelphia)
articles.author: Junius Albus
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Passing along Chestnut Street on last Sabbath afternoon, on my way to church, I noticed a prominent house on that thoroughfare, which appeared to be the headquarters for colored soldiers. Suspended at the window was a large placard, headed, "To Arms! To Arms! Colored Men!" Proceeding a few steps further, I encountered on the side-pavement a double-file of what appeared to be new recruits, with colored officers. (Pseudonymous writer; argues against drilling on the Sabbath, citing Rev. T. H. Stockton.)

articles.headline: Recruits from Indiana
articles.summary: There are quite a number of our Indiana boys who have recruited from that State, and are now out at Camp Penn. We recognized several of them, and would say to their families that they are doing well. We should be pleased to see a large number enlist from Indiana.

articles.headline: Left the City for a Few Weeks (city carrier)
articles.summary: Our city carrier, Brother A. Fields, is out of the city, and the boy whom we have employed may miss some. Therefore, if any one should fail to get his paper, he will please make a little allowance on this account, and send us word of the unlucky omission, and the paper shall be sent immediately, or, if preferable, call at our office and get it.
people: city carrier of the Christian Recorder (Brother)

articles.author: A. L. Stanford
articles.summary: On Sunday, the 12th inst., at 3 o'clock, P.M., a sermon by the pastor; theme, "Christ our life." Quarterly Meeting on Sabbath, the 19th. Quarterly Conference on Wednesday, the 15th, at 8 o'clock, P.M.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (Frankford, Pa.)
articles.summary: Acknowledgments: Canada West (Rev. L. O. Chambers, Rev. R. R. Disney, Rev. W. H. Hawkins, Rev. John Taylor, all per Bishop Nazrey); Central City, C.T. (Mrs. L. articles.headline: The Third Colored Regiment Here in the North
articles.summary: There is now at this time the third colored regiment being raised here in Philadelphia, under the auspices of that noble-hearted and humane citizen of old Massachusetts, Major Stearns, who has been empowered with the requisite authority to enlist colored men in this State, and elsewhere if he choose. ... We now appeal to the colored men of Philadelphia, and especially to the young and able-bodied. (Urges enrolment at headquarters, No. 1210 Chestnut St., between 12th and 13th; asks not less than one thousand men from the city and county.)

articles.headline: A Visit to the Colored Home of New York City
articles.summary: On Thursday, June 25th, 1863, in company with Rev. Stephen Smith of Philadelphia, and Rev. Joseph P. Shreeves of the New England Conference, we visited the Colored Home of New York for the first time in life, though the other two brethren had been there before. When we arrived we were received kindly by the matron, Mrs. Elizabeth Hagor [New York; not linked]. (Followed by 'The Colored Orphan Asylum of New York'.)

articles.headline: A Matron's Letter from Camp Barker
articles.author: Emily Howland
articles.summary: Camp Barker, Washington, June 19th, 1863. William Still, Esteemed Friend: The two valuable boxes and bundle of clothing, and the letter addressed to Miss Patton, have been passed over to me by Mr. George Baker. Will you express to your Association our gratitude for the good things they have prepared for the needy? (Thanks a Philadelphia association, through William Still, for clothing for freedpeople at Camp Barker; signed Emily Howland, Lock Box 20, Washington, D.C.)
people: addressee; forwarded clothing from a Philadelphia association to Camp Barker

articles.headline: Colored Troops, No. 3 (letter: National Hall meeting; assault on a colored soldier on Chestnut Street)
articles.author: Junius Albus
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: We were gratified to see the enthusiasm manifested at the recent meeting in National Hall, on this subject, and in perusing the remarks of Judge Kelley, Professor Bassett, Miss Dickinson, and other speakers. Times change, and we change with them; sometimes for the worse; but, in this case, for the better. Some of your readers may recollect the scenes which took place at the destruction of Pennsylvania Hall, some twenty years or more since. (Later: 'Only a day or two since, a friend informs us that he saw a ruffian advance to an inoffensive colored man, who was, with his comrades, marching along Chestnut street, and strike him a most cruel blow on the shoulder.')

articles.headline: Colored Men, Arouse!
articles.summary: The 3d Colored Regiment under the instruction of Major Stearns, is progressing finely in this city. They are coming here from all parts of the country to enlist. In Philadelphia, however, we are sorry to say, there are very few of our men enlisting. But they are like other people, they have their objections. (Urges men not to stand on dollars and cents; expects Congress to give all soldiers the same pay, bounty and rations.)

articles.headline: The Riots in New York, Resisting the Government Draft
articles.summary: The sad and painful intelligence has come to us from all quarters, of a most stubborn, lawless, malicious, ... mob of negro-haters, and negro-murderers, who violently resisted the authorities of the law for drafting men to aid in putting down this rebellion. (Contrasts the New York authorities with 'our noble hearted, dignified, gentlemanly Mayor Henry, of Philadelphia,' who 'like General Meade, is reported to be all the time on the lookout.')

articles.author: H. H. Blackston
articles.summary: The corner-stone of the A. M. E. Zion Wesley Church will be laid in Burlington, on Sunday, the 26th of July, services to commence at 2 o'clock. Rev. H. H. Blackston, Elder in Charge.

articles.headline: Glad
articles.summary: We are glad to see that the churches in Baltimore have more pride about them than the churches in Philadelphia have, except a few, and there appears to be more pride everywhere.

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting at Burlington
articles.summary: Last Sabbath we had stepped on board the steamer Trenton and sailed up to Burlington, to Rev Theodore Gould's Quarterly meeting. We arrived just before the Love-feast was out, and heard a number give testimony of the hope of that rest which remains for the children of God. It being nearly time for preaching, Elder Gould said to us that he wished us to preach and administer the Lord's Supper. (At 2 1/2 o'clock P.M. Rev. Josiah Eddy preached; about fifteen dollars raised for the elder.)
people: preacher at the Burlington quarterly meeting (Rev.)

articles.headline: Died (Sister Amelia Cregg)
articles.summary: Sister Amelia Cregg departed this life on Thursday, 23d inst., at 7 o'clock, A.M. She was a strict member of Bethel Church, and liked by all who knew her. She had something like the dropsy several months before she died, and also the asthma.
people: deceased (Sister), member of Bethel Church; died July 23, 1863

articles.headline: Notice (Quarterly Meeting of Bethel Church)
articles.summary: The Quarterly Meeting of Bethel Church comes off next Sabbath. It is to be hoped that there will be a good time.

articles.headline: The Colored Soldiers
articles.summary: The first regiment of colored soldiers of Philadelphia is, we believe, full; the second will commence immediately, if not already commenced. We shall give the names of all the men enlisted next week, if they can be got ready.

articles.headline: Lecture (B. F. Randolph at the Second Presbyterian Church, St. Mary's Street)
articles.summary: There will be a free lecture delivered in the Second Presbyterian Church in St. Mary's Street, by B. F. Randolph, of Oberlin, on Monday evening, 27th inst., at 8 o'clock, P.M. Subject: "Our country, present and future." (Lecturer from Oberlin, Ohio; not linked.)

articles.headline: Lodging (Mrs. Julia A. Brown)
articles.summary: Mrs. Julia A. Brown, No. [number illegible] South [..]th Street, is now prepared to lodge two or three respectable young men, and to give them meals on Sabbath, if desired. Information can be had of Mrs. Brown, or at the Book Store, [619] Pine Street, Philadelphia. (Ran July 4 to 25; street number illegible in all four impressions.)

people: boarding-house keeper (Mr. and Mrs.), Lombard St. between Fourth and Fifth

articles.headline: To Our Subscribers (Pennington, N.J., uncalled-for papers)
articles.summary: We are continually receiving notices from postmasters, of the neglect of many our subscribers to call for their papers. At Pennington, N. J., the postmaster has sent the names of those who have not called for them, here they are: Mrs. Caroline Early, Mary Brown, Philip Light, Rebecca M. Hall, and many others at other places in New Jersey and Baltimore.

articles.headline: Love Feast (at Bethel)
articles.summary: We were at a Love Feast on last Monday night at Bethel church, under the pastoral care of Rev. J. P. Campbell. We had a very good time. ... We noticed nothing like as many as are usually at Bethel love feasts. Where were the others?

articles.headline: A Disloyal Colonel
articles.summary: On last Monday, having walked a great deal, and feeling very tired, we were compelled to do what was a source of great humiliation to us, that is, ride on the front platform of a city passenger car. While there, a man with a long segar in his mouth, caused the car to stop and stepped upon the platform. This man was dressed in the clothes of a soldier, with epaulets, we believe, of the rank of colonel.

articles.headline: Died (Mark Davis, of Bethel)
articles.summary: Brother Mark Davis, one of Bethel's best Church members, and a local preacher I believe, departed this life on Tuesday, the 28th of July, in his 50th year. He was confined to his bed two weeks and two days with something like the diarrhea.
people: deceased; member and local preacher, Bethel Church

articles.headline: Acknowledgments
articles.summary: Boston, Mass.: Rev. G. A. Rue, for papers sold. Havre de Grace, Md.: Rev. Wm. H. Hopkins, for books. Salem, N. J.: David Russel, per Rev. J. Holden [VERIFY].

articles.headline: The Draft in Philadelphia and the Colored People
articles.summary: The draft is gradually, but certainly progressing finely, and none of the anticipated difficulty which was expected from disloyal mobites. There is one particular feature in drafting colored men which has a tendency to do harm; and that is, that each of the names of the drafted men are published, and there was a mark of retained distinction between the white draft and the colored.

articles.headline: One Price Clothing Store (Jones & Co., 604 Market St.) (puff)
articles.summary: We would call the special attention of our readers to the clothing establishment of Jones & Co., No. 604 Market street, Philadelphia. This is a first class clothing store, and can accommodate all.

articles.headline: Letter from Mount Holly (church destroyed by tornado; harvest home)
articles.author: T. Gould
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: I wish to inform your readers that our people in Mount Holly have met with a very sad accident; they having been struggling for the last three years to build a church; they had succeeded in erecting it, and enclosed it with doors and windows, which cost between six and seven hundred dollars. On Friday, July 17th, a tornado swept over the place...

articles.headline: Reply to Rev. Wm. H. Jones on B. M. E. Church
articles.author: A. R. Green
articles.summary: Bro. Weaver: Again I am called upon to defend the truth in your columns, in reply to Rev. Wm. H. Jones in No. 30 of your paper. ... The entire difficulty is whether the B. M. E. Church in 1860, had a bishop; and what acts of the General Conference did disorganize the church. Dated Philadelphia, July 27th, 1863. Quotes the committee report from p. 20 of the Philadelphia Annual Conference Minutes of 1862, signed A. L. Stanford, R. Robinson, J. P. Campbell, W. D. W. Schureman, Josiah [surname uncertain, read 'Eddy'?] [VERIFY], Committee.
people: 1862 Philadelphia Annual Conference committee member (signer of quoted report)

articles.author: William Offer
articles.summary: The Society of the Mount of Forty Days, of the A. M. E. Mt. Zion church, New Brunswick, under the pastoral charge of Wm. Offer, Rev. Wm. Moore, Elder, will celebrate their anniversary in Professor Strong's woods, on Thursday, August 20th, 1863. Dinner and refreshments will be provided on the ground.

articles.headline: Editorial Absence
articles.summary: We shall be from home for a few weeks in consequence of our attending the Western Conference, and we would say to those of our correspondents to write a little plainer if they please... Our first meeting will be at the Wilberforce College, on the 6th inst., thence on our way to the Conference, Chicago, Ill.

articles.headline: Colored Troops at Camp William Penn (parade postponed)
articles.summary: The third regiment of colored troops is now full, and there is every prospect of filling another, some three or four companies having the desired number of men. At the latter part of last week several of our daily papers published the gratifying intelligence that the Third Regiment of Philadelphia Colored troops would come into the city from Camp William Penn, to go through the evolutions of a street parade. The day came, but with it also came the postponement of the promised treat indefinitely.

articles.headline: The Editor's Experience on the City Passenger Cars
articles.author: Sea Star
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: You complain, after having walked a great deal through the city, on last Monday, of feeling tired, and having to submit to the humiliation of riding on the front platform of the car. That of itself was enough, but would not be half so humiliating if prejudice did not assign it as the only place allowable for negroes. ... In these times of great peril, we ought to have in every city protective associations.

articles.headline: Dr. P. Gardiner, Botanic Physician (advertisement)
articles.summary: Feeling grateful for the patronage received during a practice of 18 [VERIFY] years at 913 [VERIFY] Locust Street, Phila., Pa., and thinking I might still be able to assist suffering humanity, I have yielded to the persuasion of friends and will, for the present, practice at my present location, Mercer street, corner of Ewa [?] Hill, Princeton, New Jersey. ... Advice can be obtained at the above mentioned residence, or at my old residence, [9]19 [VERIFY] Locust Street. Dr. P. Gardiner, Botanic Physician.
people: botanic physician (Dr.); formerly of Locust Street, Philadelphia, now Princeton, N.J.

articles.headline: City Charges in the Summer Season
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: How unlike the white are the colored churches in the city during the hot months of Summer. At this season many of the white churches are closed, and the pastors who have been laboring with them for the last ten months are gone to some watering-place or to a country-seat with the kind approval of all their churches and congregations. Dated Philadelphia, August 10th, 1863.

articles.headline: A Man Shot (at Camp William Penn)
articles.summary: A very unfortunate and distressing occurrence took place at the colored camp at Chelton Hills on Friday night. It appears that a colored sentry who occupied the most exposed beat, and the one nearest to the public road, was accosted by a man named William Fox, about half past nine o'clock in the evening. Fox is a gardener to Mrs. Butler, who occupies the mansion in the vicinity.
people: sentry, recruit of the 6th Regiment (U.S. Colored Troops), Camp William Penn

articles.headline: The Colored People of Philadelphia
articles.summary: Many earnest inquiries are made concerning the condition of the colored people of this city, their moral, intellectual and physical condition. This is very natural and proper, for we cannot form a correct judgment until we have facts in the case. ... There are in this city 20,000 persons of color; nearly one half of this number were born south of Mason's and Dixon's line.

articles.headline: Notice: A Sabbath School Walk (A.M.E. Sabbath School, Burlington, N.J.)
articles.author: T. Gould
articles.summary: The A. M. E. Sabbath School in Burlington propose going out on an excursion in the woods on Thursday, August 20th. Dinner will be prepared in the woods for the accommodation of all present. There will be a concert in the church in the evening, given by the Princeton choir, of vocal and instrumental music.

articles.headline: Good News from the Burlington Circuit (Evesham)
articles.author: T. Gould
articles.summary: Report of a protracted and quarterly meeting at Evesham, N.J., with love feast, sacrament, and preaching by 'Brother Thomson of Philadelphia' and 'Brother Laws'; eleven persons came forward and meetings were appointed every day of the week. Dated Evesham, August 10th, 1863.

articles.headline: Letter on the flag presentation at Newbern, N.C. (colored soldiers)
articles.author: Joseph E. Williams
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: I was animated with national pride, whilst reading the daily New York Times of the 5th inst., of the proceedings of the presentation of a flag by Mary Ann Starkey, the President of the Colored Women's Union Relief Association of Newbern, N. C., to the First Colored Regiment of North Carolina Volunteers, for the United States service. Dated Philadelphia, Pa., August 5th, 1863.

articles.headline: Flag presentation by the Contraband Relief Association (Washington, D.C.), flag painted by D. B. Bowser of Philadelphia
articles.summary: At a meeting of the Contraband Relief Association, held Monday, June 1, the president suggested the propriety of raising a flag for the First District regiment colored volunteers. ... Arrangements were entered into with Mr. D. B. Bowser, a colored artist of Philadelphia. The design and appropriate motto were sent; the flag is before you to-night at a cost of one hundred and twenty-five dollars.
people: colored artist of Philadelphia; painted the regimental flag

articles.summary: The A. M. E. Church at Princeton, New Jersey, being embarrassed with a heavy debt hanging over them, intend having a harvest home in Mr. Potter's woods, on Thursday, August 27th, 1863. Dinner and refreshments will be prepared in the woods. Several short addresses will be delivered by Rev. J. P. Campbell, Rev. Gould, Mr. Longfellow, Prof. Green and other popular speakers.

articles.headline: An Epitome of the Morals of Christianity
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: In the 4th chapter and 8th verse of the Epistle of Paul to the Philippians, we have the following most interesting summary of Christian morals. Dated Philadelphia, August 18th, 1863.

M., in the Union A. M. E. Church, I propose to set forth 'The claims of Church and State' upon your humble servant.

articles.headline: A Fatal Mistake (death of John Wilson of Philadelphia at Hartford)
articles.summary: We are informed that Mr. John Wilson, of Philadelphia, who arrived in Hartford, Ct., about three or four weeks ago, on a propeller, while engaged, on Monday, the 10th inst., on board of a stone scow, was taken sick, when the captain of the vessel advised him to go below and try some whisky. (From the Anglo-African.)
people: deceased (of Philadelphia; died at Hartford, Ct.)

articles.summary: The celebration of the Horntown Sabbath School will take place on the second Thursday in September, in the woods of Mr. Ash, near the A. M. E. Church.

articles.headline: Retreat meeting, Snow Hill (notice)
articles.author: H. Davis
articles.summary: By divine permission there will be a retreat meeting held in the grove joining the A. M. E. Church, on Snow Hill, on the 6th of September next. H. Davis, Elder in charge. J. H. Long, Travelling Preacher.

articles.author: Peter Gardiner

articles.summary: A musical entertainment to be given at the First Colored Wesley Church in Lombard st., on Thursday evening, Sept. 17th, 1863, under the auspices of Mrs. Hannah Fox, by a number of little children, assisted by a number of young lady amateurs, under the musical direction of Mr. A. articles.author: H. J. Rhodes

Members and representatives are requested to be present on business of importance. By order of Wm. Cooper, G. W. S. Attest: Wm. H. Longfellow, G. W. R. S.

articles.headline: Bishop Nazrey's preaching appointments (notice)

articles.headline: Railway Injustice (from the Press)
articles.author: A Subscriber
articles.summary: We clip the following from the Press. The colored soldiers have as yet but poor encouragement to enlist and greater discouragement if drafted. In this city, where one regiment has left and the other is full, the wife or sister, perhaps mother of some one that has gone to fight for liberty, and for the fall of the rebellious South, are liable to insult and injustice daily. 'Sir: Late last night, as two friends and I were passing along Market street, we saw a colored woman fall on the railroad track alongside of the Farmers' Market House...' Philadelphia, Sept. 10th, 1863.

events.name: Star of Liberty Lodge No. 1062, G.U.O. of O.F., Snow Hill, N.J. -- presentation of swords and Bible
events.description: Letter (signed with initials, unclear) describing Snow Hill, Camden Co., N.J.: a colored settlement, nearly all owning a house and from one to twenty acres; three churches (two Methodist, one Catholic), two Sabbath schools and one public school exclusively for colored children (they having been expelled from all the white schools of the district); seven different assemblies (Masonic, Odd Fellows', Good Samaritans, Love and Charity, three old-fashioned beneficial societies, and the Young Men's Union Assembly). On Wednesday evening, June 17th, the Star of Liberty Lodge, No. 1062, G.U.O. of O.F., received from their lady friends a pair of magnificent swords and a splendid bound Bible. Introductory remarks by Mr. Isaac Marry [VERIFY], P.N.F. of United Sons of Truth Lodge, No. 1218; swords presented by Mr. Samuel Marry [VERIFY] on behalf of the ladies and received for the lodge by Mr. G. events.name: Colored men's procession for H. T. Helmbold dispersed by the Mayor (Fourth of July)
events.description: On the 4th of July a procession of colored men, musiced, uniformed and bannered, marched on behalf of Mr. H. T. Helmbold, of this city, proprietor of 'Helmbold's Extract Buchu' (white patent-medicine maker). The procession was headed by a fine (colored) brass band. Through 'some unaccountable prejudice' the Mayor was informed that such proceedings should not be allowed and had them dispersed; the Recorder judged this wrong. Mr. Helmbold paid the men notwithstanding the interruption. No marchers named. Helmbold's full-column advertisement for his Extract Buchu and other 'Genuine Preparations' (H. T. Helmbold, chemist, depot on South Tenth Street below Chestnut; the house number is not legible on the film) ran in the Recorder that same day, July 4, 1863, p. 4: clippings/CR_1863-07-04_p4_helmbold-extract-buchu-ad.jpg

events.name: Mass meeting at National Hall (recruiting colored soldiers)
events.description: 'The colored and white citizens of Philadelphia held one of the most enthusiastic meetings ever held in this city on last Monday night at National Hall.' The hall was crowded. Opened by the Hon. Judge Kelley, member of Congress, who appealed to colored citizens to come forward and enlist as soldiers; Miss Dickinson, advocate of ladies' rights, spoke next; a young man from Chicago whose name was not caught; then Frederick Douglass. Rev. Stephen Smith was appointed Chairman of the meeting, and a number of Vice-Presidents were chosen (not named). Mr. J. C. White, Jr., and Mr. O. Cato, Secretaries. (Date: the Monday before the July 11 issue.)

events.name: Soldiers' Relief Association -- weekly meetings at Bethel Church and committee to receive contributions

The following named persons are a committee to receive contributions from the friends of humanity: Mary Campbell, Harriet Bacon, Sarah Scott, Emma Williams, Amelia Brooks, Amelia Howard [VERIFY], Olivia Parker, Elizabeth Clark, Ann Ware. Church, the following persons were legally elected Trustees of said University.' Philadelphia Conference: Rev. Stephen Smith, Rev. Elisha Weaver, Rev. Anthony L. Stanford, William Scott, Henry Gordon [VERIFY], Philadelphia, Pa. Trustees not of the A.M.E. Church include Rev. William Alston, Philadelphia, Pa., and Prof. Bassett, Philadelphia, Pa. Others (text only): Rev. James A. Shorter, John Cousins, John G. Mitchell, John G. Griffin, Henry Clements, Henry S. Mount, Andrew Holland; Ohio Conference (Rev. Edward D. Davis, Rev. James A. Shorter, Rev. Lewis Woodson, Thomas E. Knox, John Cousins); Baltimore Conference (Rev. John M. Brown, Rev. Alexander W. Wayman, Rev. Henry M. Turner, James H. Davis, Thomas Greene); New England, New York, Indiana and Missouri Conferences; non-A.M.E. trustees include Frederick Douglass, John M. Langston, Prof. Charles L. Reason, Dr. James McCune Smith. Trustees to meet at Wilberforce August 6, 1863. Signed Rev. James A. Shorter, President; John G. Mitchell, Secretary.

events.name: Funeral of Mark Davis, Bethel local preacher
events.location: His residence, No. 16 [VERIFY] Byrdcoat [VERIFY] Street, then Bethel Church
events.description: Mark Davis, member and (the writer believes) local preacher of Bethel Church, died Tuesday July 28, 1863, in his 50th year, after two weeks and two days in bed with something like diarrhea. Praised for visiting and consoling the sick. Remains to be interred Sabbath, 2d inst.; funeral to meet at 1 o'clock at his residence (number and street name hard to read: 'No. 16 Byrdcoat Street' as best read) and move at 2 o'clock to Bethel church.

events.name: Quarterly meeting at Attleborough, Pa. (Bro. Laws's circuit)
events.description: The editor (Weaver) left Saturday afternoon at half past two for Attleborough to assist 'Brother Laws' with his Quarterly Meeting; stopped at the house of Sister Price, mother of the wife of Rev. James Frisby. Saturday night meeting; Sabbath morning love-feast, doors open at 8. Arrived Rev. William Moore, of Trenton, and Rev. Theodore Gould, of the Burlington Circuit, 'who also presides over Brother Laws'. Rev. Wm. Moore preached at a quarter to 11 (church and yard crowded); Rev. Bro. Gould preached at half past 2 ('the first time since his ordination as an elder'); the editor preached at night. Thanks to Sister Omer (pair of chickens), Sister Price (gooseberries) and Sister Frisby. Date computed: 'last Saturday' before Aug 1 = July 25, Sabbath July 26 (event date given as the Sabbath).
attendees: Rev.; his wife's mother Sister Price hosted the editor
of the Burlington Circuit, presiding elder over Bro. Laws; preached (Rev.)

events.name: Mount Holly, N.J. church destroyed by tornado; harvest home for rebuilding
events.description: T. Gould, Elder, reports that the Mount Holly congregation, after three years' struggle, had erected and enclosed a church (cost six to seven hundred dollars) which was destroyed by the tornado of Friday, July 17th. A harvest home for the benefit of re-erecting the building was proposed for Wednesday, August 5th.

events.name: Flag raising at Camp William Penn (Third U.S. Colored Regiment)
events.description: Editorial introduction plus reprinted account: 'Last Thursday evening an immense crowd of colored and white ladies and gentlemen left the city of Philadelphia in carriages, hacks, omnibuses, and cars' for the camp. The ceremony of raising the flag over the encampment, under the direction of the Philadelphia Supervisory Committee, took place at Chelton Hills. The regiment, 'the first fully organized regiment credited to our State', officered (white officers) incl. Col. Tilghman, Major T. W. Bardwell, Acting Quartermaster J. S. McCaughan and lieutenants (names partly cut off at the torn right margin). A train left the North Pennsylvania Railroad depot at half-past three filled with colored people. Brig. Gen. Owen present; Hon. William D. Kelley and Colonel Wagner of the 88th P.V. raised the flag; Mr. George H. Earle addressed the soldiers; Kelley also spoke. No Black Philadelphians named.

events.name: Third Regiment (colored) street parade from Camp William Penn postponed
events.description: The daily papers announced that the Third Regiment of Philadelphia colored troops would parade through the city 'last Saturday' (about Aug. 1, 1863); the parade was postponed indefinitely, to the 'grievous disappointment' of colored and white Philadelphians, many of whom would have seen relatives for the last time. Reported near-mutiny in camp. Rumors: Mayor Henry received anonymous letters and telegraphed the Secretary of War to prevent the parade; or the police were occupied with two white regiments. The editorial asks whether the government considers colored soldiers bona fide troops. 'Sea Star' (same page) asks whether Philadelphia's colored ladies and gentlemen will let the 3rd (col'd) Penn. Regiment leave for Florida without a presentation.

events.name: William Fox shot by a sentry at Camp William Penn
events.description: On a Friday night (before Aug. 15, 1863) at about 9:30 p.m., William Fox, gardener to Mrs. Butler of the nearby mansion, returning from swimming with two other men and three boys, refused to move on from the camp's most exposed post near the public road (the route of recent desertions). The sentry, Charles Ridley, a recruit of the 6th Regiment, called twice for the corporal of the guard; someone called 'Shoot them'; after warnings Ridley fired, the ball entering the right wrist and passing through the body. Post surgeon Dr. J. F. Holt [?] extracted the ball; Fox was carried to a house on Mrs. Butler's grounds and died within the hour, leaving a wife and four children. Col. Wagner examined the matter.

events.name: Statistics of the colored people of Philadelphia
events.description: Unsigned article: 20,000 persons of color in the city, nearly half born south of Mason and Dixon's line; 75 per cent of those born in the city read and write; of those between five and fifteen, sixty per cent are in school. The High School for colored youth (on Lombard St., 'a very bad location, with limited accommodations') compares well with any High School in the state; seventeen schools of lower grades (six or eight public or charity schools, the rest private or pay schools); 100 societies for the care of the sick and burial of the dead, expending $25,000 yearly, average 75 members; public property (schools, churches, halls) worth $200,000; nineteen churches (Presbyterian, Baptist, Methodist, Episcopalian), Methodists most numerous; about 150 Papists, chiefly of French descent; private property $900,000; house rents $250,000; water rents $2,500 yearly; private libraries 20,000 vols.; public libraries 4,000; newspapers 'two' [?]; seven literary societies.

events.location: a grove near Burlington, N.J.; concert in the church at Burlington
events.description: The Burlington Sabbath school, with the Baptist church invited, marched to a grove (swings, jump ropes, a table of refreshments and dinner). Addresses: Brother Thompson, of Philadelphia, first (about ten minutes); the Rev. J. H. Smith; the Rev. Shepherd Holcomb [VERIFY], afflicted and unable to stand, who spoke from his carriage. Three cheers for the President, the Union, emancipation, and colored soldiers. The school marched back to town and was dismissed by the pastor. In the evening the Princeton choir gave a concert in the church; above all expenses about eighty-six [as read] dollars realized. Signed T. Gould, Pastor, Burlington, Aug. 24th, 1863.

events.name: Flag presentation to the 6th U.S. Colored Troops at Camp William Penn
events.description: Reprinted city report ('yesterday afternoon', at five o'clock). A flag, gift of the friends of the troops, presented to the colored troops at Chelton Hills; a special train carried ladies and gentlemen from the city. Silk banner, six feet square: American eagle with 'Freedom for all'; inscription 'Sixth United States Colored Troops'; reverse 'Presented by the colored citizens of Philadelphia'. Speakers: Mr. Jacob E. White [VERIFY middle initial; perhaps Jacob C. White] first; Robert E. Purvis, aid-de-camp to Major Stearns in the recruiting service, presented the flag (speech quoted, citing Milliken's Bend, Fort Wagner and Col. Robert G. Shaw, Port Hudson) and handed it to Col. Wagner, commanding the post, who replied (two regiments of colored troops from this city now at Charleston); Mr. John Bowers then addressed the troops; Col. Wm. H. Maurice delivered the closing address. The excursionists returned to the city early in the evening.
attendees: aid-de-camp to Major Stearns; presented the flag

events.name: Musical entertainment for the organ fund, First Colored Wesley Church
events.location: First Colored Wesley Church, Lombard St., Philadelphia
events.description: Children and young lady amateurs, under the auspices of Mrs. Hannah Fox, musical direction of Mr. A. Burris; Miss A. E. Burris at the piano; proceeds toward purchasing an organ for the church.

events.name: Called meeting, Grand Tabernacle of Pennsylvania, Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity
events.description: Called meeting of the Grand Tabernacle of the State of Pennsylvania, 8 o'clock, on business of importance. By order of Wm. Cooper, G. W. S.; attest Wm. H. Longfellow, G. W. R. S. Compare the rival Westchester communication of Sept. 4 printed in the same issue, which expelled Longfellow.

events.name: Grand Tabernacle (Love and Charity) quarterly communication and election, Westchester
events.description: Opened by Rev. Bro. James Hamilton. Objection to proceeding in the presence of William H. Longfellow and Joshua P. B. Eddy, expelled from Tabernacle No. 6; they were asked to withdraw. Tabernacles represented and paying tithes and taxes: Jerusalem No. 1, St. James No. 2, Henry Brooks No. 3, Prudence No. 4, King Solomon No. 5, Celestial No. 7, Olive Branch No. 8, Stephen Smith's No. 9, King David No. 10, Athenian No. 13, W. H. Longfellow No. 17 [as read], J. P. Robinson No. 16; Isaac Emery Tab. No. 1, Boston, chartered for $4. Original charter of No. 6 declared void (removed clandestinely from their hall); No. 6 to receive a new charter. Officers for the ensuing year: G. W. Superior J. H. Smith; Vice, Sis. Sarah A. Young; Chaplain, Rev. Bro. J. Hamilton; Treasurer, James Robinson; Scribe, Nathaniel Wiggins; Assistant Scribe, Sis. Maria Cropper; Deputy Superior, Rev. Bro. J. R. Morgan; Conductress, Sis. Eliza Stokey [VERIFY]; Inner Sentinel, Nathaniel Morgan; Outer Sentinel, Jacob Johnson. District Deputies: Henry Brooks, John G. Dutton, Edward Johnson, Richard Gleaves. Next Grand Meeting at the Masonic Hall, Philadelphia. Proceedings to be published in the Anglo-African and Christian Recorder. Attest, Nathaniel Wiggins, Grand Scribe.

events.name: Quarterly meetings, Princeton Circuit (Princeton, Grigstown, Rocky Hill, the Mountain)
events.description: Second quarterly meeting at Princeton Sept. 19-20, Quarterly Conference 3 o'clock on the 19th; Grigstown Oct. 3-4; Rocky Hill Oct. 10-11; the Mountain Oct. 17-18. Peter Gardiner, Preacher in charge.

events.name: Bethel A.M.E. Church: bishop's hearing on the trustees' complaint against Rev. J. P. Campbell, and Campbell's resignation
events.location: basement of Bethel A.M.E. Church, Sixth St., Philadelphia
events.description: Called by Bishop Willis Nazrey (notice dated Sept. 6) to settle difficulties between the elder in charge and the trustees. Present: the elder in charge, trustees, official board and itinerant ministers Revs. Wm. Moore, H. Davis, J. Woodlyn, James Hollen [VERIFY], T. Gould, J. Young, J. Smith, W. D. W. Schureman and A. L. Stanford (secretary). Two documents from the trustees (dated July 16th, 1863 and Aug. 31st, 1863) were read and acknowledged. Rev. J. P. Campbell answered, giving an account of his government from May 2d, 1863. Trustee Theodore Young made a rebutting statement. Official board testimony: Solomon K. Hubert [VERIFY] (leader and steward) saw no cause for removal; Robt. Wilson (steward) not prepared to say; Major Debuty [VERIFY] (leader) no fault; Arthur Tate (leader) spoke unfavorably; Charles Bracy [VERIFY] (preacher) no cause; Josiah Eddy (deacon) said he ought to be removed as deficient as a governor; J. P. B. Eddy (elder) spoke highly in his favor; Wm. Acson [VERIFY] (preacher) said he had been misrepresented; Alfred Lawrence (leader) finances very low and membership declining but not Campbell's fault; Lyttleton Dennis (preacher) opposed removal; Thomas Todd (leader) favorable. Rising vote of the official board: seventeen that his continuance would not be injurious, one that it would. Council of itinerant ministers, Wednesday Sept. 9, resolved unanimously that no cause was shown for removal. Campbell nevertheless tendered his resignation of the charge, to take effect after Sept. 23d, 1863; Nazrey accepted it, while denying the trustees' right to close a church against a minister sent by the conference. Committee (A. L. Stanford, Wm. Moore, J. Woodlyn) reported resolutions that Campbell acted honorably and that nothing presented reflected dishonor on his government. Publication committee: Willis Nazrey, W. D. W. Schureman, A. L. Stanford. Farewell sermon announced on p2 for 'next Sunday' at 3 P.M. in Bethel.

events.name: Rev. J. P. Campbell's farewell sermon at Bethel
events.description: Farewell sermon at 3 P.M. 'next Sunday' (Sept. 20, 1863, computed from the issue date) in Bethel church; friends asked to contribute.

events.name: Zion Mission Circuit quarterly conference and meetings
events.description: Quarterly Conference at Norristown Sept. 26, 1863, 3 P.M.; quarterly meetings Norristown Sept. 27, Zion Mission Oct. 4, Germantown Oct. 11. W. D. W. Schureman, Minister.

events.name: Evesham A.M.E. Sabbath School excursion
events.description: Excursion with dinner; neighboring schools invited; addresses by Rev. J. P. Campbell and others; proceeds toward building a new church at Evesham. T. Gould, minister in charge.

events.name: Bethel official board resolutions on Elder Campbell's resignation
events.description: On motion of Henry Gordon the board regretted the circumstances causing Campbell's resignation before the time allotted, approved his administration and expressed confidence in his integrity. Statement on collections charged by some to have been kept by Campbell: Oct. 23d, 1862 for contrabands; Jan. 1st, 1863 for the poor of the church; Jan. 5th for contrabands; one sent to Campbell from Salem Circuit for the same purpose, paid over to J. H. Wright of Washington City, D.C. (receipt held); and a collection to erect a monument to Bishop Allen, said to be $69 [as read], accounted for by the Phila. Annual Conference. Signed: Alfred Lawrence, William Ackoe [VERIFY], Solomon J. Hubert [VERIFY], Peter D. Lewis, Maurice Hall, James Frisby, Robert Wilson, Littleton Dennis, Abram Fitche [VERIFY], Henry Gordon, Thomas Todd, George W. Johnston, Charles Bracey, Jacob Hardy [VERIFY], Adam Lawrence, Joshua R. Eddey [VERIFY], Lewis R. Seymour.

events.name: King Solomon Tabernacle No. 5 trial and expulsions
events.location: Masonic Hall, South Eleventh Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Tabernacle tried and expelled Joshua P. B. Eddy (late W. S.), Mary Carpenter and Israel C. Mills [VERIFY] for refusing to deliver up books, papers and other property; Elizabeth P. Longfellow (late Treasurer) for refusing to deliver up monies and property; and William H. Longfellow as having knowledge and being accessory. Signed John G. Dutton, W. S.; U. W. Brown [VERIFY], R. S. Part of the Love and Charity schism (see CR_1863-09-12).
